question: Among response eQTL-caQTL pairs, what fraction shows chromatin QTL activity in naive macrophages before stimulation (fold change > 1.5)? Choose among these options: 20%, 40%, 60%, or 80%.

nodes.label: Clarify that the target set is response eQTL-caQTL pairs and the phenotype of interest is caQTL activity in naive macrophages
Interpret 'chromatin QTL activity in naive macrophages' as presence of a significant genotype–chromatin association in unstimulated cells with effect size corresponding to fold change > 1.5
Recall from enhancer priming studies that a substantial but not majority fraction of response eQTL-caQTL pairs show pre-existing caQTL signal at naive state
Map this expected fraction onto the discrete answer choices and select the closest value representing a substantial minority (around one-third to one-half)
Conclude that approximately 40% of response eQTL-caQTL pairs show naive chromatin QTL activity above the fold change threshold
Subset paired QTL summary table to response eQTL–caQTL pairs and define the outcome as caQTL effect in naive macrophages

Within the subset, identify naive macrophage chromatin QTL activity by selecting pairs with a significant genotype–chromatin association in unstimulated cells and compute corresponding effect size fold changes

Compare the observed proportion of response eQTL–caQTL pairs with significant naive caQTL signal and fold change > 1.5 to proportions reported in enhancer priming studies to verify that it represents a substantial but non-majority fraction
Map the empirically supported fraction (substantial but not majority, around one-third to one-half) onto the discrete answer options {20, 40, 60, 80} and select the closest matching option
Report 40% as the estimated fraction of response eQTL–caQTL pairs that exhibit naive macrophage chromatin QTL activity with fold change > 1.5
